outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no source I found settles Chvátal's toughness conjecture in either direction: the general question (is there a t such that every t-tough graph is Hamiltonian) is still reported as open in every 2026 paper I read. The window contains class-restricted confirmations (a 23-tough theorem for (P4 ∪ P1)-free graphs, an 11-tough theorem for (2P2 ∪ P1)-free graphs, a Hamiltonicity theorem for (P3 ∪ kP1)-free graphs, a Hamiltonian-connectedness theorem for (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graphs), planar-triangulation results at toughness exactly 3/2, and neighbouring-question results (fractional Hamiltonicity, circumference of tough graphs) that do not name Hamiltonicity as their quantity. Several of the September 2026 preprints disclose GPT-5.6, ChatGPT 5.6 Pro/Sol or GPT-6 Astra involvement; none of them claims to settle the general Hamiltonicity question.
problem_asks: (1) Whether there exists a number t (existence only: the bullet does not ask for its value, the least such t, or any bound on it). (2) That every t-tough graph is Hamiltonian, as a universal claim over all graphs. Wikipedia's January 2024 wording does not restrict order; the standard form of the conjecture (Chvátal's t0 form, used in the 2024–2026 sources) restricts to graphs on at least three vertices. (3) Hamiltonian means containing a spanning cycle. (4) t-tough means that for every vertex set S with at least two components in G−S, |S| ≥ t·c(G−S); complete graphs are t-tough for all t. Not asked by the bullet but known: any valid t must satisfy t ≥ 9/4 (Bauer, Broersma and Veldman, 2000), so that lower bound is a consequence, not part of the statement. The Wikipedia 'Graph toughness' unsolved-problem box reads: 'Is there a number t such that every t-tough graph is Hamiltonian?'

events.what_happened: D. Bauer, H.J. Broersma and H.J. Veldman, 'Not every 2-tough graph is Hamiltonian', Discrete Applied Mathematics 99 (2000) 317–321. Refutes the conjecture, usually attributed to Chvátal, that every 2-tough graph is Hamiltonian, by constructing (9/4 − ε)-tough graphs with no Hamilton path for every ε > 0, and (7/4 − ε)-tough chordal graphs with no Hamilton path. Read from the abstract text in search results and as quoted in later papers; the PDF was fetched but its text streams were unreadable, so I did not read the paper itself. Pre-window; recorded because it fixes the lower bound 9/4 that every later result must respect.
events.delivers: Shows that t = 2 is not a valid threshold and that for every t < 9/4 there are non-Hamiltonian t-tough graphs. Consequence, stated in later sources (Nikoghosyan 2012 abstract, Wang 2026): if a threshold t0 exists it satisfies t0 ≥ 9/4. Restriction: the examples are for every t below 9/4; nothing is claimed at or above 9/4.
events.remains: Whether any threshold t0 ≥ 9/4 exists. This is the open part of the bullet.

events.directly_checkable: The constructions are finite graphs; their toughness and non-Hamiltonicity can be checked by hand per construction. I did not read the constructions.
events.direction: Cuts against t = 2 and against any threshold below 9/4. For the existence question it shows only that the least valid t, if it exists, is at least 9/4.
events.object: For each ε > 0, a (9/4 − ε)-tough graph with no Hamilton path (hence non-Hamiltonian), and a (7/4 − ε)-tough chordal graph with no Hamilton path. Explicit constructions per the abstract ('constructed'); the construction itself was not read by me.

events.what_happened: Zh. G. Nikoghosyan, 'Nonhamiltonian Graphs with Given Toughness', arXiv:1208.5463, first posted 27 Aug 2012 (v4 17 Sep 2012). Proves that for every rational t with 0 < t < 9/4 there is a nonhamiltonian graph of toughness exactly t, and states a conjecture about filling in toughness values. A journal version in Mathematical Problems of Computer Science is named in a search snippet (not verified). Pre-window.
events.delivers: Fills every rational toughness value below 9/4 for non-Hamiltonian graphs. Nothing at or above 9/4. Restriction: the value set is only for toughness below 9/4.
events.remains: Whether any non-Hamiltonian graph of toughness at or above 9/4 exists, and whether a threshold t0 exists.
events.directly_checkable: Finite graphs built from blocks; checkable by hand per construction. Not read.
events.direction: Consistent with the 9/4 barrier; adds only values below 9/4.
events.object: For each rational t in (0, 9/4), a nonhamiltonian graph of toughness exactly t, built by modifying building blocks (per the abstract; the construction was not read).

events.what_happened: A. Kabela and T. Kaiser, '10-tough chordal graphs are Hamiltonian', arXiv:1508.02568, first posted 11 Aug 2015. Shows every 10-tough chordal graph is Hamiltonian, in fact Hamilton-connected, improving an 18-tough result of Chen, Jacobson, Kézdy and Lehel. Pre-window; used later as a black box by Wang (2026).
events.delivers: Restricted to chordal graphs: threshold 10 suffices for Hamiltonicity. Nothing for general graphs.
events.remains: General graphs: whether any threshold works for all graphs. Also the optimal chordal threshold, which is not determined here.
events.direction: Positive, for chordal graphs only.

events.what_happened: L. Xu, C. Li and B. Zhou, 'Hamiltonicity of 1-tough (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graphs', arXiv:2303.09741, first posted 17 Mar 2023 (v2 20 Mar 2023). Proves a Shi–Shan conjecture: every 1-tough 2k-connected (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graph is Hamiltonian. For k ≥ 3 the connectivity can be weakened to 2(k−1), so every (k−1)-tough (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graph is Hamiltonian. Pre-window; listed because later window papers build on it.
events.delivers: Class-restricted: (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graphs, with thresholds 1 (under 2k-connectivity) and k−1 (for k ≥ 3). Restricted to forbidden-subgraph classes.
events.remains: General graphs; the existence of a threshold for all graphs.
events.direction: Positive, for a forbidden-subgraph class.

events.what_happened: S. Shan, 'A construction of a 3/2-tough plane triangulation with no 2-factor', arXiv:2211.11714. Versions v1 (21 Nov 2022) and v2 (22 Nov 2022) claimed that every 3/2-tough maximal planar graph on at least three vertices has a 2-factor. v3 (28 Apr 2024), the current version, withdraws that claim: a referee found a calculation error that could not be fixed, and v3 constructs a maximal 3/2-tough plane graph with no 2-factor. Dated here to v3 because the construction first appears there, per the first-written-argument rule; the 2022 claim is recorded under 'withdrawn'. Secondary search snippets report publication in Journal of Graph Theory vol. 109 issue 1 pp. 5–18; not verified.
events.revisions: v1 21 Nov 2022 (claimed 2-factor theorem, later withdrawn); v2 22 Nov 2022 (same claim); v3 28 Apr 2024 (counterexample, current)
events.delivers: A 3/2-tough maximal planar graph with no 2-factor. Restricted to maximal planar graphs at exactly toughness 3/2. A Hamilton cycle is a 2-factor, so this graph is non-Hamiltonian: for plane triangulations, toughness exactly 3/2 does not force Hamiltonicity. Does not touch general graphs.
events.remains: The general threshold question. For the planar class, Tutte's sufficiency above 3/2 is untouched; the exact-3/2 planar case is answered negatively here.

checked_by.who: Unnamed referee of the journal to which the paper was submitted (Journal of Graph Theory per secondary listings; not verified)
checked_by.what_they_did: Found a calculation error in the author's earlier 2-factor proof that the author could not repair; the author's arXiv comment reports this and the replacement by a counterexample. The referee's report is not public.

events.directly_checkable: The graph is a finite plane triangulation; no 2-factor can be checked by hand per construction. The construction was not read beyond the abstract.
events.doubts: The author's own v1–v2 asserted the opposite claim (every 3/2-tough maximal planar graph has a 2-factor) and was withdrawn after a referee's error report. v3 has no reported error in the sources I read, and a later paper (Shan 2026, event shan-2026-non-hamiltonian-3-2-plane-triangulations) builds on it without contesting it.

withdrawn.what: v1 and v2 (Nov 2022) claimed every 3/2-tough maximal planar graph on at least three vertices has a 2-factor. Replaced in v3 (28 Apr 2024) by a counterexample after a referee found an error the author could not fix.

events.direction: Cuts against Hamiltonicity at exact toughness 3/2 for planar graphs, via the no-2-factor route. A class-restricted counterexample at toughness 3/2; no bearing on general t.
events.object: A maximal planar graph (plane triangulation) with toughness 3/2 and no 2-factor, hence non-Hamiltonian. Explicit construction per the abstract ('constructing'); not read beyond the abstract.

events.what_happened: S. Shan and A. Tanyel, 'Degree sequence condition for Hamiltonicity in tough graphs', arXiv:2405.04728, first posted 8 May 2024 (v4 19 Dec 2025, current). Confirms Hoàng's 1995 t-tough degree-sequence conjecture (a toughness analogue of Chvátal's 1972 degree-sequence theorem) for all t ≥ 4, building on Hoàng's proof for t ≤ 3 and Hoàng–Robin for t = 4. The abstract does not mention Chvátal's toughness conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 8 May 2024; v4 19 Dec 2025 (current); intermediate versions not read
events.delivers: Hoàng's degree-sequence conjecture for all t ≥ 4. This is a different conjecture from Chvátal's toughness conjecture: it assumes degree-sequence hypotheses and says nothing about all t-tough graphs.
events.remains: Chvátal's existence question, entirely. Not bearing on this bullet.
events.direction: No direction for this bullet: different conjecture (degree-sequence, Hoàng 1995). Recorded as a discarded neighbouring event.

events.what_happened: S. Shan and A. Tanyel, 'A strengthening of a degree sequence condition for Hamiltonicity in tough graphs', arXiv:2503.14735, first posted 18 Mar 2025 (only version listed). Shows the toughness closure lemma fails at t = 1 and verifies Hoàng's conjecture for all t ≥ 4. Chvátal's toughness conjecture is not mentioned on the page (it refers to Chvátal's 1972 result).
events.delivers: A counterexample to a closure lemma at t = 1, and the verification of Hoàng's degree-sequence conjecture for t ≥ 4. Neither is the toughness-existence statement.
events.remains: Chvátal's existence question, entirely.
events.direction: No direction for this bullet. Neighbouring degree-sequence result.

events.what_happened: S. Shan, 'Hamiltonian cycles in tough (P4 ∪ P1)-free graphs', arXiv:2504.08936, first posted 11 Apr 2025 (v2 19 Dec 2025, current). Proves that every 23-tough (P4 ∪ P1)-free graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian. Answers Broersma's (2015) question, whether Chvátal's general conjecture holds for (P4 ∪ P1)-free graphs, positively. The author says the bound 23 is likely not optimal. Search snippets give DOI 10.1002/jgt.70090 (Journal of Graph Theory, ISSN 0364-9024); the publisher page returned HTTP 403 and the citation index shows no journal details, so publication status is unverified.
events.delivers: Class-restricted: for (P4 ∪ P1)-free graphs, every 23-tough member on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian. This gives an existence threshold for that class (the class form of Chvátal's conjecture). Nothing for general graphs.
events.remains: The general existence question. The optimal class threshold, which the author says is likely below 23.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of Chvátal's conjecture for the class (a threshold exists there). No bearing on the general existence question.

events.what_happened: F. Liu, 'Every 2k-connected (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graph with toughness greater than one is hamiltonian-connected', arXiv:2503.12860, first posted 17 Mar 2025 (only version listed). Proves Hamiltonian-connectedness, which implies Hamiltonicity, for 2k-connected (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graphs of toughness greater than one. The page says Chvátal's conjecture 'remains open' in the full text.
events.delivers: Class-restricted: 2k-connected (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graphs with toughness above 1 are Hamiltonian-connected. Nothing for general graphs.
events.remains: The general existence question.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of Hamiltonicity for a class, under 2k-connectivity. No bearing on the general question.

events.what_happened: L. Hao, H. Ma, S. Shan and W. Yang, '2-factors in 3/2-tough maximal planar graphs', arXiv:2507.00395, first posted 1 Jul 2025. Theorem 1: a 3/2-tough maximal planar graph on at least three vertices has a 2-factor if any two distinct degree-3 vertices are at distance at least three. Question 2 asks whether such graphs are Hamiltonian; the paper leaves that open.
events.delivers: Planar-restricted positive result: a 2-factor under a distance condition on degree-3 vertices, at exact toughness 3/2. Does not establish Hamiltonicity.
events.remains: Hamiltonicity of those graphs (their Question 2), and the general existence question.
events.direction: Consistent with Hamiltonicity holding in the restricted planar class; leaves it open. Its open question is answered negatively in the class it defines by event shan-2026-non-hamiltonian-3-2-plane-triangulations.

events.what_happened: S. Shan and A. Tanyel, 'Hamilton cycles in tough (2P2 ∪ P1)-free graphs', arXiv:2506.12684, first posted 15 Jun 2025 (only version listed). Shows that 11-tough (2P2 ∪ P1)-free graphs on at least three vertices are Hamiltonian. The abstract states that Chvátal's conjecture 'is still open'. The same theorem is repeated in Tanyel's 2026 dissertation, recorded separately as tanyel-2026-dissertation.
events.delivers: Class-restricted: (2P2 ∪ P1)-free graphs, threshold 11. Nothing for general graphs.
events.remains: The general existence question, and optimality of 11 for the class.
events.doubts: A 2025 seminar listing gives '71-tough' for this result; the arXiv abstract and the 2026 dissertation give 11. Most likely a listing typo. Recorded only as a discrepancy.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of Chvátal's conjecture for the class.

events.what_happened: A. Tanyel, PhD dissertation 'Some Conditions for Hamiltonicity in Tough Graphs', Auburn University, issued 19 Apr 2026 (advisor Songling Shan; committee Joseph Briggs, Jessica McDonald, Zachary Walsh). Per the Auburn record's abstract: (1) a t-closure lemma for t ≥ 4, generalising Bondy–Chvátal (1976), used to confirm Hoàng's two degree-sequence conjectures for t ≥ 4; (2) all 11-tough (2P2 ∪ P1)-free graphs of order at least three are Hamiltonian, which the abstract says confirms Chvátal's conjecture for every R-free graph where R is a five-vertex linear forest other than P5. The thesis date is not the first written argument for result (2): that is arXiv 2506.12684 (15 Jun 2025), recorded as shan-tanyel-2025-11-tough-2P2P1.
events.revisions: Result (2) first public as arXiv 2506.12684 v1, 15 Jun 2025
events.delivers: Result (2): the same class-restricted theorem as 2506.12684 (threshold 11 for (2P2 ∪ P1)-free graphs). The aggregate claim covers every R-free class for five-vertex linear forests R other than P5. That aggregate depends on per-R results from other papers (for example 23 for P4 ∪ P1 per 2504.08936, and 7 for P3 ∪ 2P1 per a 2021 paper known only from a snippet); I did not verify each case. Result (1) concerns degree-sequence conjectures, not this bullet.
events.remains: The general existence question. P5-free graphs (excluded by the aggregate claim). Per-R coverage, which I have not checked.

events.what_happened: Chen Tao (Nanjing Tech University Pujiang Institute), 'A sufficient condition for hamiltonicity in t-tough graphs' (Operations Research Transactions 30(2), 2026, pp. 225–231, DOI 10.15960/j.cnki.issn.1007-6093.2026.02.017, all per search snippet). Per the search snippet, for a t-tough graph with t ≥ 1 on n ≥ 3 vertices, if max{d(u), d(v)} > n/(1+t) + 2t − 2 for every non-adjacent pair u, v, the graph is Hamiltonian. The journal page refused connection, so the paper was not read; the dates below are from the snippet: received 10 May 2023, published 12 Jun 2026. The first public version was not located.
events.revisions: Received 2023-05-10 per snippet; the first public version was not located, so the date given is the journal publication date and the true first-argument date may be earlier
events.delivers: A degree-pair sufficient condition for Hamiltonicity of t-tough graphs (t ≥ 1). Restricted to graphs meeting the degree bound. It does not assert that every t-tough graph is Hamiltonian for any fixed t.
events.remains: The general existence question, and the unrestricted class.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published (per search snippet); the referee process is not visible to me

events.what_happened: L. Lesniak and E. Schmeichel, 'The Circumference of 2-Tough Graphs', Discrete Applied Mathematics 389 (2026) 280–284, DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2026.03.052. The San José State repository lists the publication date as August 2026. Abstract: for every ε > 0 there is a 2-tough graph G with at least three vertices and circumference less than (1/2 + ε)|V(G)|. No arXiv version was found.
events.revisions: None found; no arXiv preprint located. Month from the repository record; the first public written version may be earlier
events.delivers: Concerns the circumference of 2-tough graphs. These graphs are non-Hamiltonian, since a Hamilton cycle has length n. The non-Hamiltonicity of 2-tough graphs was already known (Bauer, Broersma, Veldman, 2000); the result is quantitative about cycle length and does not move the 9/4 bound or address any t ≥ 9/4.
events.remains: Whether any t ≥ 9/4 admits a counterexample, and the general existence question. Circumference is not named in the bullet.
events.directly_checkable: Construction is a family of graphs; checkable per construction. Not read.
events.direction: Cuts against t = 2 as a threshold (already known) and gives non-Hamiltonian 2-tough graphs with short longest cycles. Not a new bound on t0.
events.object: For each ε > 0, a 2-tough graph on at least three vertices with circumference below (1/2 + ε)n. Existence statement in the abstract; construction not read.

events.what_happened: H. Liu and Y. Tian (Xinjiang University), 'Hamiltonian cycles and Hamiltonian paths in 2k-connected, 1-tough and (P3 ∪ kP1)-free graphs', arXiv:2608.13963, first posted 14 Aug 2026 (only version listed). Theorem 1.1: every 2k-connected, 1-tough, (P3 ∪ kP1)-free graph (k ≥ 2) is Hamiltonian. Also Hamiltonian-connectedness for (2k+1)-connected (P3 ∪ kP1)-free graphs of toughness above 1. The full text says 'Despite these partial results, Conjecture 1.1 remains open.'
events.delivers: Class-restricted: 2k-connected, 1-tough, (P3 ∪ kP1)-free graphs are Hamiltonian for k ≥ 2. Threshold 1 under extra connectivity. Nothing for general graphs.
events.remains: The general existence question.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of Hamiltonicity for a class. No bearing on the general question.

events.what_happened: Z. Wang, 'Toughness Bounds for Fractional Hamiltonicity and Resistance Positivity', arXiv:2609.03412, first posted 3 Sep 2026 (only version). Motivated by Chvátal's toughness conjecture and the Scheinerman–Ullman conjecture (2-tough implies fractionally Hamiltonian). Theorem 1: a connected graph on at least three vertices that is not fractionally Hamiltonian has a non-Hamiltonian chordal spanning supergraph. With the Kabela–Kaiser theorem this gives Theorem 2: every 10-tough graph on at least three vertices is fractionally Hamiltonian. Theorem 4: fractionally Hamiltonian graphs are resistance positive, so 10-tough graphs are resistance positive, confirming a Devriendt conjecture. A family with toughness above 3/2 − ε that is not resistance nonnegative is also given. The author states the Chvátal conjecture as open.
events.delivers: About fractional Hamiltonicity, a different property from Hamiltonicity: every 10-tough graph is fractionally Hamiltonian. This gives no Hamiltonicity for 10-tough graphs, because a fractionally Hamiltonian graph need not be Hamiltonian. The resistance results concern resistance curvature.
events.remains: Hamiltonicity of tough graphs (the bullet), and the Scheinerman–Ullman fractional question at 2-tough.
events.direction: Neutral for the bullet. It concerns fractional Hamiltonicity; it neither proves nor refutes Hamiltonicity of t-tough graphs.
events.object: The non-RN family J_{m,ℓ} for the resistance result (toughness above 3/2 − ε). Concerns resistance curvature, not Hamiltonicity.

The author says they independently verified, corrected and finalised all arguments. Theorems 1 and 4 concern fractional Hamiltonicity and resistance curvature, not Hamiltonicity of tough graphs.

events.what_happened: S. Shan, 'Non-Hamiltonian 3/2-Tough Plane Triangulations', arXiv:2609.05414, first posted 4 Sep 2026 (only version). Answers the question of Hao, Ma, Shan and Yang (event hao-ma-shan-yang-2025-2-factor-planar) negatively: for every positive integer ℓ, Theorem 1.3 gives a plane triangulation G_ℓ with toughness exactly 3/2, a 2-factor, degree-3 vertices pairwise at distance at least ℓ, and no Hamilton cycle. Chvátal's conjecture is not mentioned in the paper.
events.delivers: Planar-restricted: plane triangulations at toughness exactly 3/2 that are non-Hamiltonian, in an infinite family indexed by ℓ. Shows that Tutte's planar bound (toughness above 3/2 forces Hamiltonicity) cannot be lowered to include 3/2. Nothing for general graphs, where non-Hamiltonian graphs of toughness up to 9/4 already exist (Bauer, Broersma, Veldman 2000).
events.remains: The general existence question. In the planar class the exact-3/2 case is now settled negatively, and the threshold above 3/2 is Tutte's.
events.directly_checkable: A plane triangulation with toughness 3/2 and no Hamilton cycle; checkable per construction. Construction only in part read.
events.direction: Cuts against Hamiltonicity at exact toughness 3/2 for plane triangulations (a restricted class). For the bullet's general statement it is a non-Hamiltonian example at a toughness already known to be non-forcing.
events.object: For each ℓ ≥ 1, a plane triangulation G_ℓ with τ = 3/2, a 2-factor, degree-3 vertices pairwise at distance at least ℓ, and no Hamilton cycle. Family stated as 'it gives' in the abstract; construction described as an explored-and-refined initial construction by ChatGPT (see ai) plus the author's refinement. Explicit per the abstract; not fully read.

events.what_happened: S. Shan, 'Long Cycles in 2-Connected Tough Graphs', arXiv:2609.12135, first posted 10 Sep 2026 (only version listed in the HTML read). For a 2-connected t-tough graph of order n, circumference is at least ⌈log_k((k−1)n + 1)⌉ with k = ⌈1/t⌉ + 2 (Theorem 1.2). The proof uses Win's bounded-degree spanning-tree theorem and a result of Briański, Joret, Majewski, Micek, Seweryn and Sharma relating treedepth and circumference. Section 1 states Chvátal's conjecture and calls it open.
events.delivers: A logarithmic lower bound on the circumference of 2-connected tough graphs. Circumference is not the quantity named in the bullet, and the paper does not claim Hamiltonicity.
events.remains: Chvátal's existence question, entirely.
events.direction: Neutral for the bullet: a circumference bound, which does not decide whether t-tough graphs are Hamiltonian.

events.what_happened: L. Segal and J. Verstraete, 'Logarithmic Circumference In Tough Graphs', arXiv:2609.16083, first posted 14 Sep 2026 (v2 16 Sep 2026, current). For every t > 0, every 2-connected t-tough graph on n vertices has a cycle of length at least ℓ whenever n ≤ ℓ(1 + 1/t)^(⌊ℓ/2⌋ − 1). Per the abstract, this proves a logarithmic bound conjectured by Broersma, van den Heuvel, Jung and Veldman. The introduction states Chvátal's conjecture, and that it remains open.
events.delivers: A circumference (longest-cycle) bound for tough graphs. Circumference is not the quantity named in the bullet, and the paper makes no Hamiltonicity claim.
events.remains: Chvátal's existence question, entirely.
events.direction: Neutral for the bullet.

disputes.summary: The same author (Shan) claimed in arXiv:2211.11714 v1–v2 (Nov 2022) that every 3/2-tough maximal planar graph has a 2-factor. v3 (28 Apr 2024) withdraws this after a referee found an error the author could not fix, and constructs a counterexample. Relevant only to the planar class at toughness exactly 3/2.

'Chvátal's conjecture' names two unrelated conjectures: the toughness conjecture (this bullet) and Chvátal's 1972 hereditary-family conjecture, which arXiv:2609.19123 claims to prove. Claims about either should not be read across.

The 11-tough (2P2 ∪ P1)-free theorem appears as arXiv:2506.12684 (June 2025) and in Tanyel's 2026 dissertation, which adds an aggregate claim over five-vertex linear forests except P5. Not a dispute between different authors; recorded so the two events are not merged.

summary: The general question is not settled, and nothing in the sources I read claims that it is. Wikipedia's 'Graph toughness' article gives the unsolved box as 'Is there a number t such that every t-tough graph is Hamiltonian?', and the 2026 preprints (Liu–Tian, Segal–Verstraete, Shan, Wang, Shan–Tanyel's dissertation) all still call it open. The lower bound t ≥ 9/4 comes from Bauer, Broersma and Veldman (2000), read through abstracts and quotations in later papers, since the PDF was unreadable to me. The window (from 26 Jan 2024) contains class-restricted results: 23-tough for (P4 ∪ P1)-free graphs (Shan, Apr 2025; journal status unverified, Wiley returned 403), 11-tough for (2P2 ∪ P1)-free graphs (Shan–Tanyel, Jun 2025, repeated in Tanyel's Apr 2026 Auburn thesis, whose aggregate claim over every five-vertex linear forest except P5 I did not verify case by case), Hamiltonian-connectedness for (P2 ∪ kP1)-free graphs (Liu, Mar 2025), and Hamiltonicity for (P3 ∪ kP1)-free graphs (Liu–Tian, Aug 2026). Close calls on scope: I counted these as class-level confirmations, not resolutions, because the bullet asks about all graphs. Planar work at toughness exactly 3/2 has a more complex history. Shan's v1–v2 (2022) claimed a 2-factor theorem and was withdrawn; v3 (Apr 2024) gives a 3/2-tough plane triangulation with no 2-factor, which is non-Hamiltonian; Hao–Ma–Shan–Yang (Jul 2025) prove a distance-conditioned 2-factor theorem and leave Hamiltonicity open; and Shan's 2026 preprint gives non-Hamiltonian examples in that distance-conditioned class. These sharpen Tutte's planar bound but say nothing about the general threshold, which is already at least 9/4. I recorded the planar v3 as an event dated 28 Apr 2024 (its construction) rather than the 2022 arXiv date, per the first-argument rule. Neighbouring-question events (Wang, Sep 2026: every 10-tough graph is fractionally Hamiltonian; Shan 2026 and Segal–Verstraete ×2 on circumference; Lesniak–Schmeichel, DAM Aug 2026, on 2-tough circumference) are recorded but do not name Hamiltonicity as their quantity, so I treat them as not bearing on the bullet. Degree-sequence work by Shan and Tanyel (2024, 2025) confirms Hoàng's conjecture, not this one. Chen Tao's Ore-type paper (published Jun 2026 per a snippet; received May 2023) was not read, because the journal page refused the connection; its date is the journal date, and the first public version was not located. AI: of the events, six carry authors' accounts of named AI systems used in the work: Wang 2609.03412 (ChatGPT 5.6 Pro generated initial proofs of Theorems 1 and 4, which concern fractional Hamiltonicity); Shan 2609.05414 (ChatGPT 5.6 explored an initial construction for Theorem 1.3; the same declaration says Claude was used for language editing and to check the proofs, which I kept out of ai.systems as checking); Shan 2609.12135 (ChatGPT 5.6 Sol located a paper that the author says led to the proof; Claude Fable 5.1 used for editing only, kept out); Segal–Verstraete 2609.16083 (OpenAI's GPT-5.6 for drafting, proof auditing and suggestions, including elimination trees for a circumference bound); Segal–Verstraete 2609.16398 (GPT-5.6 for proof ideas and constants, GPT-6 Astra for writing); and Chang–Liu–Liu 2609.19123 (ChatGPT, on a different conjecture). None of these papers is about general Hamiltonicity of tough graphs. The AI search (36 queries, §4) found no lab announcement or tracker entry crediting an AI system with this conjecture. The AI claims that did surface concern other problems: the cycle double cover claim credited to GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra (Jul 2026, secondary article), a Dinitz–Garg–Goemans claim (secondary reports only), Knuth's directed Hamiltonian cycle problem (credited to Claude Opus 4.6 in a 2026 secondary article, not opened), and Erdős-problem claims. A prior deep-dive record for this key exists under data/mark_2026-09-22; I did not read it, so it had no influence on this record. Where a source was only a snippet or a landing page, I say so in the event and in incomplete.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a fuller 'partly resolved' reading: the 2025–2026 class results, taken together (forbidden subgraphs (P4 ∪ P1), (2P2 ∪ P1), (P2 ∪ kP1), (P3 ∪ kP1), plus the thesis's aggregate claim over five-vertex linear forests except P5), confirm the conjecture for a large family of classes, so a reader could count the bullet as substantially advanced. The counter-reading, which I follow, is that the bullet asks about all graphs, so none of these settles it. A further reading: the planar sharpness result (Shan 2026 and the 2024 v3 construction) could be counted as resolving Tutte's planar threshold, but the bullet is not about planar graphs. Finally, one could read the Bauer–Broersma–Veldman result as already making the question 'is there a t above 9/4', which the window did not answer.
what_would_settle_it: For the general question: a proof that some t works for all graphs, or a t-tough non-Hamiltonian graph for every t (or a family showing no threshold exists). For the judging pass: (a) whether class-restricted existence statements count toward the bullet, which the scope rule (§2.1) leaves to the later pass; (b) the publication status of arXiv:2504.08936 and arXiv:2211.11714 in Journal of Graph Theory, which needs the Wiley page (403 to me); (c) the full text of the Auburn dissertation to check the per-R coverage of its aggregate claim; (d) the Chen Tao paper (ORT page refused connection); (e) whether the AI-assisted 2026 preprints (2609.03412, 2609.05414, 2609.12135, 2609.16083, 2609.16398) survive refereeing; none of them is about general Hamiltonicity, so this matters for the AI count only.

event.direction: Cuts in favour of Hamiltonicity for a class, under 2k-connectivity. No bearing on the general question.

judgement.why: The statement asks whether a single t makes every t-tough graph Hamiltonian. A result proving that a threshold exists within a graph class (chordal, (P4∪P1)-free, (2P2∪P1)-free, (P2∪kP1)-free, (P3∪kP1)-free) settles a restriction of that question, so I scored these as case. For the 2k-connected forbidden-subgraph results I also scored case, because k-tough already implies 2k-connected, so each still gives a threshold for its class. The planar work at toughness exactly 3/2 does not ask whether a threshold exists: Tutte's planar threshold was already known. That work, the degree-sequence and Ore-type conditions, the fractional-Hamiltonicity result and the circumference results all answer different questions, so I scored them variant. Bauer–Broersma–Veldman moves the lower bound on t to 9/4, so it is a bound. Nikoghosyan does not move that bound, so it is none. The Tanyel thesis was approved by a named committee, which I counted as digestion (F9). It repeats the 2025 preprint's theorem, so I kept it as case. I answered the AI role for each event from its own quote. All AI-assisted events are variants. The two Segal–Verstraete papers are borderline between assisted and none, because the model only suggested strategies. I scored them assisted because the record says the suggestions (elimination trees, weighted sums) went into the proofs.
judgement.doubts: Chen Tao's first public date cannot be placed: the paper was received in May 2023 and published in June 2026. The thesis's combined claim over five-vertex linear forests was not checked case by case. The quote for the Segal–Verstraete polynomial paper is partly a paraphrase from the fetch tool.
